record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical two-dimensional conformal field theory
record.original_question: Let V be a simple vertex operator algebra such that V(0)=C1, V(n)=0 for n<0, the contragredient V-module V' is equivalent to V, and V is C2-cofinite, meaning dim V/C2(V)<infinity where C2(V) is spanned by Res_x x^-2 Y(u,x)v for u,v in V and Y is the vertex operator map. Is the braided tensor category of grading-restricted generalized V-modules constructed from logarithmic tensor-category theory rigid?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.1. Assume that V is a simple vertex operator algebra satisfying the following conditions: (1) V(0) = C1, V(n) = 0 for n < 0 and the contragredient V', as a V-module, is equivalent to V.

(2) V is C2-cofinite, that is, dim V/C2(V) < infinity, where C2(V) is the subspace of V spanned by the elements of the form Res_x x^-2Y(u,x)v for u, v in V and Y : V tensor V -> V[[x, x^-1]] is the vertex operator map for V. Then the braided tensor category given in [H8] based on the work [HLZ1]-[HLZ9] is rigid.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let V be a simple vertex operator algebra over C with vertex operator map Y: V ⊗ V → V[[x, x^{-1}]] and grading V = ⊕_{n∈Z} V_(n). Assume:

(1) V_(0) = C·1, V_(n) = 0 for n < 0, and the contragredient module V' is isomorphic to V as a V-module;

(2) V is C_2-cofinite, meaning dim(V / C_2(V)) < ∞, where C_2(V) is the subspace of V spanned by all elements of the form Res_x x^{-2} Y(u, x)v for u, v ∈ V.

Under these assumptions, the category of grading-restricted generalized V-modules carries a braided tensor category structure constructed via logarithmic tensor-category theory (the Huang–Lepowsky–Zhang construction).

Question: Is this braided tensor category necessarily rigid? That is, does every object X admit a (left and right) dual X^∨ together with evaluation and coevaluation morphisms satisfying the usual zig-zag identities?
artifact.category_tag: Vertex operator algebras and tensor categories
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is known to hold in the rational case (when V is also regular/rational, by Huang's theorem giving a modular tensor category). In the non-semisimple (logarithmic) C_2-cofinite setting, rigidity has been established only under additional hypotheses: notably, McRae proved that rigidity holds provided the S-transform of the character of V is a linear combination of characters of V-modules (and related conditional results, including factorizability once rigidity is assumed). The general conjecture without extra assumptions appears to remain open as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: On rationality for C_2-cofinite vertex operator algebras (McRae)
status_evidence.snippet: For a C_2-cofinite VOA V, if the S-transformation of the character of V is a linear combination of characters of V-modules, then the category of grading-restricted generalized V-modules is rigid; assuming rigidity, the category is a factorizable finite ribbon (non-semisimple modular) tensor category.
status_evidence.claim: Rigidity for C_2-cofinite logarithmic tensor categories has been proven under an additional hypothesis on the S-transformation of the character, but not in general.

status_evidence.title: Rigidity and modularity of vertex tensor categories (Huang)
status_evidence.snippet: For C_2-cofinite rational VOAs, the category of V-modules is a rigid modular tensor category.
status_evidence.claim: The rigidity statement is established in the rational subcase.

status_evidence.title: C1-cofiniteness and vertex tensor categories
status_evidence.snippet: Recent works continue to study rigidity questions for vertex tensor categories arising from C_n-cofinite VOAs.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues; the general conjecture is not closed.
